chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who speaks forgetfully during the salat (prayer), saying, "Straighten your rows." He said: "He completes his salat (prayer), then performs two sajdahs." I said: "Are the two sajdahs of forgetfulness before the taslim or after it?" He said: "After it."

key_terms.أَقِيمُوا صُفُوفَكُمْ: straighten your rows; the example phrase spoken during prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.بَعْدَهُ: after it; indicating the timing after the taslim
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations of forgetfulness performed to remedy an error in prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: two prostrations required as corrective sajdahs
key_terms.نَاسِيًا: forgetfully; speaking unintentionally due to forgetfulness
key_terms.يُتِمُّ صَلَاتَهُ: he completes his prayer without restarting it

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he speaks forgetfully during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who speaks forgetfully during salat (prayer). The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer is completed and then two sajdahs of forgetfulness are performed after the taslim.
